    Class DiContainer

    Enhanced dependency injection container with automatic constructor injection support. Supports singleton registration, factory registration, type bindings, and automatic dependency resolution.

    Inheritance

    Namespace: GameFramework.Core
    Assembly: .dll
    Syntax
    public class DiContainer
    Remarks

    This DI container provides three main registration patterns:

    • Singleton: One instance created and reused for all requests
    • Transient: New instance created for each request
    • Factory: Custom factory function called for each request

    The container automatically resolves constructor dependencies using reflection, selecting the constructor with the most parameters and recursively resolving all dependencies. Circular dependency detection prevents infinite resolution loops.

    Design Benefits: Clean separation of concerns, automatic dependency resolution, easy testing, loose coupling
    Trade-offs: Runtime dependency resolution, potential circular dependencies, reflection overhead

    Examples
    // Register services
container.RegisterSingleton<ILogger, ConsoleLogger>();
container.RegisterTransient<IRepository, DatabaseRepository>();
container.RegisterFactory<IConnection>(() => new SqlConnection(connectionString));

// Resolve services (automatic constructor injection)
var service = container.Resolve<IMyService>();

    Clear()

    Clears all registrations from the container.

    public void Clear()

    This method removes all singleton instances, factories, type bindings, and clears the resolution stack. Primarily useful for testing scenarios where you need to reset the container state between tests.

    RegisterFactory<T>(Func<T>)

    Registers a factory function that creates new instances on each resolution request.

    Declaration
    public void RegisterFactory<T>(Func<T> factory) where T : class
    Parameters
    Type Name Description
    Func<T> factory

    The factory function that creates instances of T.
    Type Parameters
    Name Description
    T

    The service type to register.
    Remarks

    Use factory registration when you need custom creation logic, configuration, or when each request should receive a fresh instance with specific setup. The factory function is called every time the service is resolved.

    Examples
    container.RegisterFactory<IDatabase>(() => new SqlDatabase(GetConnectionString()));
container.RegisterFactory<IHttpClient>(() => new HttpClient { Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30) });
    Exceptions
    Type Condition
    ArgumentNullException

    Thrown when factory is null.

    RegisterSingleton<TInterface, TImplementation>()

    Registers a singleton mapping from interface to implementation type. The instance will be created on first request using constructor injection.

    Declaration
    public void RegisterSingleton<TInterface, TImplementation>() where TImplementation : class, TInterface
    Type Parameters
    Name Description
    TInterface

    The service interface type.
    TImplementation

    The concrete implementation type.
    Remarks

    The implementation instance is created lazily on first request and then cached for all subsequent requests. Constructor dependencies are automatically resolved.

    Examples
    container.RegisterSingleton<IUserService, DatabaseUserService>();
// First call creates instance, subsequent calls return cached instance
var service1 = container.Resolve<IUserService>();
var service2 = container.Resolve<IUserService>(); // Same instance as service1

    RegisterTransient<TInterface, TImplementation>()

    Registers a transient type binding where a new instance is created for each request.

    Declaration
    public void RegisterTransient<TInterface, TImplementation>() where TImplementation : class, TInterface
    Type Parameters
    Name Description
    TInterface

    The service interface type.
    TImplementation

    The concrete implementation type.
    Remarks

    Transient services create a new instance every time they are requested. Use this for stateless services or when you need isolated instances. Constructor dependencies are automatically resolved for each new instance.

    Examples
    container.RegisterTransient<IEmailService, SmtpEmailService>();
// Each resolution creates a new instance
var email1 = container.Resolve<IEmailService>();
var email2 = container.Resolve<IEmailService>(); // Different instance than email1

    Resolve<T>()

    Resolves a service instance of type T using automatic constructor injection.

    Declaration
    public T Resolve<T>() where T : class
    Returns
    Type Description
    T

    An instance of type T with all dependencies injected.
    Type Parameters
    Name Description
    T

    The service type to resolve.
    Remarks

    This is the primary method for retrieving services from the container. The container automatically resolves constructor dependencies recursively. Resolution order: singleton instances → factories → type bindings → direct creation.

    Examples
    // Assuming UserService has constructor: UserService(ILogger logger, IDatabase db)
var userService = container.Resolve<IUserService>();
// Logger and Database are automatically injected
    Exceptions
    Type Condition
    InvalidOperationException

    Thrown when the service is not registered and cannot be created directly, or when a circular dependency is detected.
